correctness.rationale: An independent symbolic four-labelled-person absorption calculation, starting from masks (susceptible, infected)=(14,1) and using payoff 4 minus the susceptible count at absorption, reproduces both endpoint values and derivatives for symbolic b, the full rational G_4, the eight-degree derivative numerator, all nine transformed coefficients, and the exact positive difference 295591073/32512225144680. The quartic has one sign change and takes opposite signs at 3 and 4. The denominator of G_b'(1) is positive and the numerator is minus b times this quartic, so adding within-patch contact (decreasing epsilon from 1) has the reported signs. Also G_b'(0)>0; for b>b_* neither endpoint maximizes the continuous mean. At b=4 the substitution t=epsilon/(1-epsilon) gives exactly one coefficient sign change and opposite signs at zero and infinity. With the original positive denominator this gives exactly one strict global maximum, not just one located critical point. In the equal one-person-per-patch case the only potential secondary infection competes directly with the seed recovery, giving the strictly increasing function in the record. The row sums fix the nominal disease-free next-generation spectral radius at b throughout.
residual_risks: The next-generation radius is the defined disease-free linearized quantity, not a realized secondary case count. At b=b_* only the first derivative is shown to vanish. The unique global maximizer is proved at b=4, not for general b>b_*. No inference beyond this stylized four-person model.

value.rationale: A fixed-radius reversal is a meaningful counterexample to a mixing monotonicity heuristic. The exact transmission threshold identifies when this reversal is possible at the endpoint; the degree-eight uniqueness certificate and minimal equal-patch population put analytic, not merely numerical, limits on the example. The gain in mean size is tiny, but its mathematical value is the strict sign and provable threshold, not a claimed practical improvement.
residual_risks: Not an empirical travel, contact, or larger-population recommendation.
